## Deck Goal
Explain in under three minutes that probabilistic model proposals require deterministic policy and capability boundaries, with confidential-computing attestation as a separate resource-release guarantee.

## Required Background
{
  "deck_context": {
    "audience": "Google DevFest Sydney 2026 engineering audience",
    "core_claim": "Don't put guarantees inside the prompt. Put guarantees around the model.",
    "factual_limits": [
      "PLAYBOOK.md and model proposals are untrusted.",
      "Python PolicyEngine evaluates authoritative state and policy.",
      "CapabilityGate controls a fixed simulated executor set.",
      "DENY means the executor is never called.",
      "The attack is a controlled deterministic example, not an observed live Gemini result.",
      "Gemini inference remains remote and outside this project's TEE.",
      "This checkout contains no current live cloud-attestation evidence."
    ]
  }
}

## Global Style
{
  "name": "minimal editorial engineering conference",
  "visual_direction": "carefully hand-crafted PowerPoint with Apple-keynote clarity; flat, precise, quiet, and strongly typographic",
  "canvas": "16:9 warm white #FAF9F6",
  "color_palette": "near-black #111111 and one muted amber #B7791F accent only",
  "typography": "clean modern sans-serif, two weights maximum, large and projector-readable",
  "density": "very sparse with generous whitespace and one idea per slide",
  "avoid": "photos, illustration, AI imagery, gradients, shadows, texture, 3D, decorative geometry, icon collections, cards, fake terminals, logos, watermarks, slide numbers"
}
